card.name: Defect conditions leading to discard
card.fires_on: The comma or helping word right after an 'if' clause naming a defect (leaks, particles, discoloration, damaged port) in inspection instructions. It marks the spot where 'discard' or 'do not use' is expected.

modes.label: Comma after defect clause
modes.description: Comma closing an 'If ... damaged/present/found' clause before the discard instruction.
modes.example: If particulates or discoloration are present<<,>> discard the bag.

modes.label: Helper word before 'not be used'
modes.description: The word 'should' or 'be' after a product with particles, just before an instruction not to use it.
modes.example: Preparations of bivalirudin for injection containing particulate matter<< should>> not be used.

card.writes: It pushes toward words about preventing or stopping something, such as 'prevent' and 'before'.
card.plain: It fires where a label has just described a visible defect and is about to say to throw the product away.
